sentences.zh: 方今內有朱虛、東牟之親，外畏吳、楚、淮陽、琅邪、齊、代之強。

translations.literal: Now within there are kin such as Zhu Xu and Dong Mou; without, they fear the strength of Wu, Chu, Huaiyang, Langye, Qi, and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Now within there are kin such as Zhu Xu and Dong Mou; without, they fear the strength of Wu, Chu, Huaiyang, Langye, Qi, and Dai.

sentences.zh: 方今高帝子，獨淮南王與大王。

translations.literal: Among the High Emperor's sons today, only the King of Huainan and Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Among the High Emperor's sons today, only the King of Huainan and Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 大王又長，賢聖仁孝聞於天下，故大臣因天下之心而欲迎立大王。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is moreover the eldest; your worth, sagacity, humanity, and filial piety are heard throughout all under Heaven—therefore the great ministers rely on the hearts of all under Heaven and wish to welcome and establish Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is moreover the eldest; your worth, sagacity, humanity, and filial piety are heard throughout the realm—therefore the great ministers rely on the hearts of the realm and wish to welcome and establish Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 大王勿疑也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty must not doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must not doubt.

sentences.zh: 」代王報太后計之。

translations.literal: " The King of Dai reported to the empress dowager to work out a plan.
translations.idiomatic: " The King of Dai reported to the empress dowager to work out a plan.

sentences.zh: 猶豫未定，卜之，兆得大橫。

translations.literal: Still hesitating and undecided, he divined; the omen obtained Great Horizontal.
translations.idiomatic: Still hesitating and undecided, he divined; the omen obtained Great Horizontal.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「大橫庚庚，余為天王，夏啟以光。

translations.literal: The interpretation said: "Great Horizontal, geng geng; I become King of Heaven; Xia Qi with brightness.
translations.idiomatic: The interpretation said: "Great Horizontal, geng geng; I become King of Heaven; Xia Qi with brightness.

sentences.zh: 」代王曰：「寡人固已為王矣，又何王？

translations.literal: " The King of Dai said: "I am already king—what further kinghood?
translations.idiomatic: " The King of Dai said: "I am already king—what further kinghood?"

sentences.zh: 」卜人曰：「所謂天王者，乃天子也。

translations.literal: " The diviner said: "What is called King of Heaven is in fact the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " The diviner said: "What is called King of Heaven is in fact the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」於是代王遣太后弟薄昭往見絳侯，絳侯等具為昭言所以迎立王意。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the King of Dai sent the empress dowager's younger brother Bo Zhao to go see the Marquis of Jiang; Bo and the others fully explained to Zhao the reason for welcoming and establishing him as king.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the King of Dai sent the empress dowager's younger brother Bo Zhao to see the Marquis of Jiang; Bo and the others fully explained to Zhao the reason for welcoming and establishing him as king.

sentences.zh: 薄昭還報曰：「信矣，無可疑者。

translations.literal: When Bo Zhao returned and reported, he said: "It is trustworthy; there is nothing to doubt.
translations.idiomatic: When Bo Zhao returned and reported, he said: "It is trustworthy; there is nothing to doubt.

sentences.zh: 」代王乃笑謂宋昌曰：「果如公言。

translations.literal: " The King of Dai then smiled and said to Song Chang: "It has indeed been as you said.
translations.idiomatic: " The King of Dai then smiled and said to Song Chang: "It has indeed been as you said.

sentences.zh: 乃命宋昌參乘，張武等六人乘傳，從詣長安。

translations.literal: He then ordered Song Chang to ride as companion, Zhang Wu and six others to travel post-haste, and followed to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Song Chang to ride as companion, Zhang Wu and six others to travel post-haste, and followed to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 至高陵，休止，而使宋昌先馳之長安觀變。

translations.literal: Reaching Gaoling, he stopped to rest and sent Song Chang first to gallop to Chang'an and observe developments.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Gaoling, he stopped to rest and sent Song Chang first to gallop to Chang'an and observe developments.

sentences.zh: 昌至渭橋，丞相以下皆迎。

translations.literal: When Chang reached the Wei Bridge, the chancellor and those below all came to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang reached the Wei Bridge, the chancellor and those below all came to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 昌還報。

translations.literal: Chang returned to report.
translations.idiomatic: Chang returned to report.

sentences.zh: 代王馳至渭橋，群臣拜謁稱臣，代王下車答拜。

translations.literal: The King of Dai galloped to the Wei Bridge; the ministers bowed in audience and styled themselves subjects; the King of Dai descended from the chariot and returned the bows.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Dai galloped to the Wei Bridge; the ministers bowed in audience and styled themselves subjects; the King of Dai descended from the chariot and returned the bows.

sentences.zh: 太尉勃進曰：「願請間。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Bo advanced and said: "I wish to request a private word.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Bo advanced and said: "I wish to request a private word.

sentences.zh: 」宋昌曰：「所言公，公言之；

translations.literal: " Song Chang said: "What you would speak is public—speak it publicly;
translations.idiomatic: " Song Chang said: "What you would speak is public—speak it publicly;

sentences.zh: 所言私，王者無私。

translations.literal: what is private, a king has no private affairs.
translations.idiomatic: what is private, a king has no private affairs.

sentences.zh: 」太尉乃跪上天子璽、符。

translations.literal: " The Grand Commandant then knelt and presented the Son of Heaven's seal and tally.
translations.idiomatic: " The Grand Commandant then knelt and presented the Son of Heaven's seal and tally.

sentences.zh: 代王謝曰：「至代邸而議之。

translations.literal: The King of Dai declined, saying: "Let us deliberate at the lodging for Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Dai declined: "Let us deliberate at the lodging for Dai.

sentences.zh: 後九月，己酉晦，代王至長安，舍代邸，群臣從至邸。

translations.literal: In the intercalary ninth month, on jiyou, the last day of the month, the King of Dai reached Chang'an, lodged at the lodging for Dai, and the ministers followed him to the lodging.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary ninth month, on jiyou, the last day of the month, the King of Dai reached Chang'an, lodged at the lodging for Dai, and the ministers followed him to the lodging.

sentences.zh: 丞相陳平等皆再拜言曰：「子弘等皆非孝惠子，不當奉宗廟。

translations.literal: Chancellor Chen Ping and all twice bowed and said: "Hong and the others are none of them sons of Emperor Xiaohui and ought not to tend the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Chen Ping and all twice bowed and said: "Hong and the others are none of them sons of Emperor Xiaohui and ought not to tend the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 大王，高帝長子，宜為嗣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, eldest son of the High Emperor, should be the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, eldest son of the High Emperor, should be the heir.

sentences.zh: 願大王即天子位。

translations.literal: We wish Your Majesty to assume the Son of Heaven's place at once.
translations.idiomatic: We wish Your Majesty to assume the Son of Heaven's place at once.

sentences.zh: 」代王西鄉讓者三，南鄉讓者再，遂即天子位。

translations.literal: " The King of Dai declined facing west three times, declined facing south twice, and then assumed the Son of Heaven's place.
translations.idiomatic: " The King of Dai declined facing west three times, declined facing south twice, and then assumed the Son of Heaven's place.

sentences.zh: 群臣以禮次侍。

translations.literal: The ministers waited in attendance according to ritual order.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers waited in attendance according to ritual order.

sentences.zh: 東牟侯興居曰：「誅呂氏，臣無功，請得除宮。

translations.literal: Marquis of Dongmou Xingju said: "In executing the house of Lü, your servant had no merit; I request to be allowed to clear the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Dongmou Xingju said: "In executing the house of Lü, your servant had no merit; I request to be allowed to clear the palace.

sentences.zh: 」乃與太僕汝陰侯滕公入宮，前謂少帝曰：「足下非劉氏子，不當立！

translations.literal: " He then entered the palace with Grand Coachman Marquis of Ruyin Teng Gong, went forward and said to the Young Emperor: "Your Excellency are not of the house of Liu and ought not to be enthroned!
translations.idiomatic: " He then entered the palace with Grand Coachman Marquis of Ruyin Teng Gong, went forward and said to the Young Emperor: "Your Excellency are not of the house of Liu and ought not to be enthroned!"

sentences.zh: 」乃顧麾左右執戟者掊兵罷去；

translations.literal: " Then he turned and gestured to those at the left and right holding halberds to cast aside weapons and withdraw;
translations.idiomatic: " Then he turned and gestured to those at the left and right holding halberds to cast aside weapons and withdraw;

sentences.zh: 有數人不肯去兵，宦者令張釋諭告，亦去兵。

translations.literal: several men would not lay down weapons; Chamberlain Zhang Shizhi was ordered to announce, and they too laid down weapons.
translations.idiomatic: several men would not lay down weapons; Chamberlain Zhang Shizhi was ordered to announce, and they too laid down weapons.

sentences.zh: 滕公乃召乘輿車載少帝出。

translations.literal: Teng Gong then summoned the imperial carriage to carry the Young Emperor out.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Gong then summoned the imperial carriage to carry the Young Emperor out.

sentences.zh: 少帝曰：「欲將我安之乎？

translations.literal: The Young Emperor said: "Where do you mean to take me?
translations.idiomatic: The Young Emperor said: "Where do you mean to take me?"

sentences.zh: 」滕公曰：「出就舍。

translations.literal: " Teng Gong said: "Go out to the lodging.
translations.idiomatic: " Teng Gong said: "Go out to the lodging.

sentences.zh: 」舍少府。

translations.literal: " He lodged him at the Minor Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: " He lodged him at the Minor Treasury.

sentences.zh: 乃奉天子法駕迎代王於邸，報曰：「宮謹除。

translations.literal: Then with the Son of Heaven's formal equipage he welcomed the King of Dai from the lodging and reported: "The palace has been carefully cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Then with the Son of Heaven's formal equipage he welcomed the King of Dai from the lodging and reported: "The palace has been carefully cleared.

sentences.zh: 」代王即夕入未央宮。

translations.literal: " The King of Dai that evening entered Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: " The King of Dai that evening entered Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 有謁者十人持戟衛端門，曰：「天子在也，足下何為者而入？

translations.literal: Ten chamberlains holding halberds guarded the main gate, saying: "The Son of Heaven is within; what are Your Excellency doing entering?
translations.idiomatic: Ten chamberlains holding halberds guarded the main gate: "The Son of Heaven is within; what are Your Excellency doing entering?"

sentences.zh: 」代王乃謂太尉。

translations.literal: " The King of Dai thereupon spoke to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: " The King of Dai thereupon spoke to the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 太尉往諭，謁者十人皆掊兵而去，代王遂入。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant went to announce; the ten chamberlains all cast aside weapons and left; the King of Dai then entered.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant went to announce; the ten chamberlains all cast aside weapons and left; the King of Dai then entered.

sentences.zh: 夜，拜宋昌為衛將軍，鎮撫南北軍；

translations.literal: At night, Song Chang was appointed General of the Guard, pacifying the Northern and Southern Armies;
translations.idiomatic: At night, Song Chang was appointed General of the Guard, pacifying the Northern and Southern Armies;

sentences.zh: 以張武為郎中令，行殿中。

translations.literal: Zhang Wu was made Gentlemen-of-the-Palace and patrolled within the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wu was made Gentlemen-of-the-Palace and patrolled within the palace halls.

sentences.zh: 有司分部誅滅梁、淮陽、恆山王及少帝於邸。

translations.literal: The relevant officials in divisions executed the kings of Liang, Huaiyang, and Hengshan and the Young Emperor at their lodging.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant officials in divisions executed the kings of Liang, Huaiyang, and Hengshan and the Young Emperor at their lodging.

sentences.zh: 文帝還坐前殿，夜，下詔書赦天下。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen returned and took his seat in the front hall; at night he issued an edict amnestying all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen returned and took his seat in the front hall; at night he issued an edict amnestying the realm.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，庚戌，徙琅邪王澤為燕王；

translations.literal: In winter of year 1, the tenth month, on gengxu, King Ze of Langye was moved to be King of Yan;
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the first year, in the tenth month, on the day gengxu, King Ze of Langye was transferred to be King of Yan;

sentences.zh: 封趙幽王子遂為趙王。

translations.literal: King You of Zhao's son Sui was enfeoffed as King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: King You of Zhao's son Sui was enfeoffed as King of Zhao.

sentences.zh: ----2陳平謝病。

translations.literal: ----2 Chen Ping declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 Chen Ping declined office on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 上問之，平曰：「高祖時，勃功不如臣，及誅諸呂，臣功亦不如勃，願以右丞相讓勃。

translations.literal: The Emperor questioned him; Ping said, “In Gaozu's time Bo's merit was not as great as mine, and in executing the Lü clan my merit was also not as great as Bo's; I wish to yield the right chancellorship to Bo.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked him; Chen Ping said, “Under Gaozu, Bo's merit was less than mine, and in executing the Lü clan mine was also less than his; I wish to yield the right chancellorship to Bo.

sentences.zh: 」十一月，辛巳，上徙平為左丞相，太尉勃為右丞相，大將軍灌嬰為太尉。

translations.literal: ” In the eleventh month, on xinsi, the Emperor moved Ping to left chancellor, Grand Commandant Bo to right chancellor, and Grand General Guan Ying to grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: ” In the eleventh month, on xinsi, the Emperor made Chen Ping left chancellor, Grand Commandant Zhou Bo right chancellor, and Grand General Guan Ying grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 諸呂所奪齊、楚故地，皆復與之。

translations.literal: The former lands of Qi and Chu seized by the Lü clan were all restored to them.
translations.idiomatic: The former Qi and Chu territories seized by the Lü clan were all restored.

sentences.zh: ----3論誅諸呂功，右丞相勃以下益戶、賜金各有差。

translations.literal: ----3 In assessing merit for executing the Lü clan, from Right Chancellor Bo downward households were increased and gold bestowed, each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 When rewards were apportioned for executing the Lü clan, from Right Chancellor Bo downward each received added households and gold according to rank.

sentences.zh: 絳侯朝罷趨出，意得甚。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Jiang, after court was dismissed, hurried out, greatly pleased with himself.
translations.idiomatic: After court the Marquis of Jiang hurried out, looking very pleased with himself.

sentences.zh: 上禮之恭，常目送之。

translations.literal: The Emperor treated him with respect and often saw him off with his gaze.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor treated him with deference and often watched him leave.

sentences.zh: 郎中安陵袁盎諫曰：「諸呂悖逆，大臣相與共誅之。

translations.literal: Palace Gentleman Yuan Ang of Anling remonstrated, saying, “The Lü clan were rebellious; the great ministers together executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Gentleman Yuan Ang of Anling remonstrated: “The Lü clan rebelled and the great ministers joined to execute them.

sentences.zh: 是時丞相為太尉，本兵柄，適會其成功。

translations.literal: At that time the chancellor was grand commandant and originally held military authority; he happened to coincide with its success.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the chancellor had been grand commandant and already held military authority; he simply happened to be there when it succeeded.

sentences.zh: 今丞相如有驕主色，陛下謙讓。

translations.literal: Now if the chancellor shows the air of a proud master while Your Majesty is deferential,
translations.idiomatic: Now if the chancellor acts like a proud master while Your Majesty defers to him,

sentences.zh: 臣主失禮，竊為陛下弗取也！

translations.literal: minister and lord lose propriety—I privately deem this unworthy for Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: lord and minister lose all propriety—I cannot think this fitting for Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 」後朝，上益莊，丞相益畏。

translations.literal: ” Afterward at court the Emperor grew more stern and the chancellor more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: ” After that at court the Emperor grew sterner and the chancellor more afraid.

sentences.zh: ----4十二月，詔曰：「法者，治之正也。

translations.literal: ----4 In the twelfth month an edict said, “Law is the straightedge of governance.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In the twelfth month an edict said, “Law is the straightedge of rule.

sentences.zh: 今犯法已論，而使無罪之父母、妻子、同產坐之，及為收帑，朕甚不取！

translations.literal: Now when one who violated the law has already been judged, yet innocent parents, wife and children, and household members of the same estate are made to share guilt, and there is confiscation of kin into servitude—We greatly disapprove!
translations.idiomatic: When the guilty have already been sentenced, yet innocent parents, wives and children, and household kin are punished with them, and families are confiscated into servitude—We cannot accept this!

sentences.zh: 其除收帑諸相坐律令。

translations.literal: Let the statutes on confiscation of kin and collective punishment be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Abolish the statutes on confiscation of kin and collective punishment.

sentences.zh: 」----5春，正月，有司請蚤建太子。

translations.literal: ” ----5 In spring, the first month, the responsible officials asked to establish the crown prince early.
translations.idiomatic: ” ----5 In spring, the first month, officials asked that the crown prince be established at once.

sentences.zh: 上曰；

translations.literal: The Emperor said;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said;

sentences.zh: 「朕既不德，縱不能博求天下賢聖有德之人而禪天下焉，而曰豫建太子，是重吾不德也。

translations.literal: “We lack virtue; even if We cannot broadly seek worthy and sage men of virtue throughout the realm and yield the realm to them, yet to speak of establishing the crown prince in advance is to double Our want of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: “I lack virtue; even if I cannot seek out worthy and sage men throughout the realm and yield the throne to one of them, to speak of establishing an heir in advance only doubles my want of virtue.

sentences.zh: 其安之！

translations.literal: Let the matter rest!
translations.idiomatic: Let the matter rest!

sentences.zh: 」有司曰：「豫建太子，所以重宗廟、社稷，不忘天下也。

translations.literal: ” The officials said, “Establishing the crown prince in advance is to give weight to the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain and not forget the realm.
translations.idiomatic: ” The officials said, “Establishing an heir in advance gives weight to the ancestral temple and altars of state and shows that the realm is not forgotten.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「楚王，季父也；

translations.literal: ” The Emperor said, “The King of Chu is Our uncle;
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor said, “The King of Chu is my uncle;

sentences.zh: 吳王，兄也；

translations.literal: the King of Wu is Our elder brother;
translations.idiomatic: the King of Wu is my elder brother;

sentences.zh: 淮南王，弟也，豈不豫哉？

translations.literal: the King of Huainan is Our younger brother—are they not already in the succession?
translations.idiomatic: the King of Huainan is my younger brother—are they not already in line?

sentences.zh: 今不選舉焉，而曰必子，人其以朕為忘賢有德者而專於子，非所以憂天下也！

translations.literal: Now not to choose among them but to say it must be a son—men will take Us as forgetting the worthy and virtuous and fixating on Our son; this is not how to care for the realm!
translations.idiomatic: If I do not choose among them but insist it must be a son, people will think I have forgotten the worthy and virtuous and fix on my own son—this is not how to care for the realm!

sentences.zh: 」有司固請曰：「古者殷、周有國，治安皆千餘歲，用此道也。

translations.literal: ” The officials pressed their request, saying, “In antiquity Yin and Zhou held their states and peace and order each lasted more than a thousand years by using this way.
translations.idiomatic: ” The officials pressed on: “In antiquity Yin and Zhou each held their states in peace for more than a thousand years by this very method.

sentences.zh: 立嗣必子，所從來遠矣。

translations.literal: Establishing the succession must be through a son—the origin of this is far back.
translations.idiomatic: The heir must be a son—a practice of very ancient standing.

sentences.zh: 高帝平天下為太祖，子孫繼嗣世世不絕，今釋宜建而更選於諸侯及宗室，非高帝之志也。

translations.literal: Gaozu settled the realm and became Grand Ancestor; descendants succeeding in generation after generation without end—now to set aside what ought to be established and instead choose anew among feudal lords and the imperial clan is not Gaozu's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu pacified the realm as Grand Ancestor so that descendants might succeed generation after generation without end; to set aside what ought to be done and choose anew among feudal lords and the imperial clan is not Gaozu's intent.

sentences.zh: 更議不宜。

translations.literal: Further discussion is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Further debate is out of place.

sentences.zh: 子啟最長，純厚慈仁，請建以為太子。

translations.literal: The son Qi is eldest, pure, generous, and benevolent—I ask that he be established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi is the eldest, pure, generous, and benevolent; we ask that he be made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 」上乃許之。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor then assented.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor then agreed.

sentences.zh: ----6三月，立太子母竇氏為皇后。

translations.literal: ----6 In the third month the crown prince's mother, the Dou clan, was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In the third month the crown prince's mother, Lady Dou, was made empress.

sentences.zh: 皇后，清河觀津人。

translations.literal: The empress was a native of Guanjin in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was from Guanjin in Qinghe commandery.

sentences.zh: 有弟廣國，字少君，幼為人所略賣，傳十餘家，聞-{竇后}-立，乃上書自陳。

translations.literal: She had a younger brother Guangguo, styled Shaojun, who in youth was kidnapped and sold, passing through more than ten households; hearing that -{竇后}- had been established, he then submitted a memorial stating his case.
translations.idiomatic: She had a younger brother Guangguo, styled Shaojun, who as a child was kidnapped and sold through more than ten households; when he heard Empress Dou had been established, he submitted a memorial identifying himself.

sentences.zh: 召見，驗問，得實，乃厚賜田宅、金錢，與兄長君家於長安。

translations.literal: Summoned and received, questioned and verified—the facts were true; he was then richly granted fields, dwellings, and gold and silver, and together with his elder brother Changjun was housed in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned, questioned, and the facts verified; he received rich grants of land, houses, and money, and he and his elder brother Changjun were given residences in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 絳侯、灌將軍等曰：「吾屬不死，命乃且縣此兩人。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Jiang, General Guan, and others said, “If our kind do not die, our lives still hang by these two men.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Jiang, General Guan, and others said, “If we are not to die, our lives still hang by these two.

sentences.zh: 兩人所出微，不可不為擇師傅、賓客；

translations.literal: The two men's origins are humble; tutors and retainers must be chosen for them;
translations.idiomatic: Both come from humble origins; tutors and retainers must be chosen for them;

sentences.zh: 又復效呂氏，大事也！

translations.literal: if they again imitate the Lü clan, it will be a great matter!
translations.idiomatic: if they imitate the Lü clan again, it will be a grave matter!

sentences.zh: 」於是乃選士之有節行者與居。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon men of learning with integrity in conduct were chosen to dwell with them.
translations.idiomatic: ” Scholars of proven integrity were then chosen to live with them.

sentences.zh: 竇長君、少君由此為退讓君子，不敢以尊貴驕人。

translations.literal: Dou Changjun and Shaojun thereby became modest gentlemen and did not dare to act proudly toward others on account of their exalted rank.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Changjun and Shaojun thereby became modest gentlemen and did not presume on their rank to treat others arrogantly.

sentences.zh: ----7詔振貸鰥、寡、孤、獨、窮困之人。

translations.literal: ----7 An edict granted relief loans to widowers, widows, orphans, solitaries, and those in destitution.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 An edict ordered relief for widowers, widows, orphans, the childless elderly, and the destitute.

sentences.zh: 又令：「八十已上，月賜米、肉、酒；

translations.literal: It also ordered: “Those eighty and above shall monthly receive rice, meat, and wine;
translations.idiomatic: It also ordered: “Those eighty and above shall receive monthly allotments of rice, meat, and wine;

sentences.zh: 九十已上，加賜帛、絮。

translations.literal: those ninety and above shall additionally receive silk and wadding.
translations.idiomatic: those ninety and above shall additionally receive silk and cotton wadding.

sentences.zh: 賜物當稟鬻米者，長吏閱視，丞若尉致；

translations.literal: Where gifts should be reported and converted to rice for sale, chief officials shall inspect; the assistant or commandant shall deliver;
translations.idiomatic: Where stipends are to be reported and converted to rice, chief officials shall inspect and the assistant or commandant shall deliver;

sentences.zh: 不滿九十，嗇夫、令史致；

translations.literal: those not yet ninety, the district clerk and recorder shall deliver;
translations.idiomatic: for those under ninety, the district clerk and recorder shall deliver;

sentences.zh: 二千石遣都吏循行，不稱者督之。

translations.literal: officials of two thousand dan shall send capital clerks to tour and inspect, and supervise those who fall short.
translations.idiomatic: officials of two thousand dan shall send inspectors on circuit and hold accountable any who fail to comply.

sentences.zh: 」----8楚元王交薨。

translations.literal: ” ----8 King Yuan of Chu, Jiao, died.
translations.idiomatic: ” ----8 King Yuan of Chu, Liu Jiao, died.

sentences.zh: ----9夏，四月，齊、楚地震，二十九山同日崩，大水潰出。

translations.literal: ----9 In summer, the fourth month, Qi and Chu had earthquakes; twenty-nine mountains on the same day collapsed and great floods burst forth.
translations.idiomatic: ----9 In summer, the fourth month, Qi and Chu were shaken by earthquakes; twenty-nine mountains collapsed on the same day and great floods burst out.

sentences.zh: ----10時有獻千里馬者。

translations.literal: ----10 At that time someone presented a horse of a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: ----10 At that time someone presented a thousand-li horse.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「鸞旗在前，屬車在後，吉行日五十里，師行三十里。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, “The imperial escort banners go before and the attendant chariots follow behind; on an auspicious journey one covers fifty li a day, on a military march thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, “Imperial banners go before and attendant chariots follow; on a ceremonial journey we cover fifty li a day, on campaign thirty.

sentences.zh: 朕乘千里馬，獨先安之？

translations.literal: If We ride a horse of a thousand li, where would We go ahead alone?
translations.idiomatic: If I ride a thousand-li horse, where would I go ahead alone?

sentences.zh: 」於是還其馬，與道里費，而下詔曰：「朕不受獻也。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he returned the horse, gave traveling expenses, and issued an edict saying, “We do not accept presentations.
translations.idiomatic: ” He returned the horse, gave traveling expenses, and issued an edict: “I do not accept presentations.

sentences.zh: 其令四方毋求來獻。

translations.literal: Let the four quarters be ordered not to seek to come with offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Let the four quarters be ordered not to come bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 」----11帝既施惠天下，諸侯、四夷遠近歡洽。

translations.literal: ” ----11 Once the Emperor had extended favor throughout the realm, feudal lords and the four Yi near and far were harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: ” ----11 Once the Emperor had extended his grace throughout the realm, feudal lords and the four quarters near and far were at ease.

sentences.zh: 乃修代來功，封宋昌為壯武侯。

translations.literal: He then reviewed merit from coming from Dai and enfeoffed Song Chang as Marquis of Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He then reviewed those who had aided his coming from Dai and enfeoffed Song Chang as Marquis of Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: ----12帝益明習國家事。

translations.literal: ----12 The Emperor grew ever clearer and practiced in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: ----12 The Emperor grew ever more skilled in affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 朝而問右丞相勃曰：「天下一歲決獄幾何？

translations.literal: At court he asked Right Chancellor Bo, saying, “Throughout the realm, how many cases are decided in a year?
translations.idiomatic: At court he asked Right Chancellor Zhou Bo: “How many cases are decided throughout the realm in a year?

sentences.zh: 」勃謝不知。

translations.literal: ” Bo apologized that he did not know.
translations.idiomatic: ” Bo apologized that he did not know.

sentences.zh: 又問：「一歲錢穀出入幾何？

translations.literal: He asked again, “How much money and grain go in and out in a year?
translations.idiomatic: He asked again: “How much money and grain enter and leave the treasury in a year?

sentences.zh: 」勃又謝不知，惶愧，汗出沾背。

translations.literal: ” Bo again apologized that he did not know, fearful and ashamed, sweat soaking his back.
translations.idiomatic: ” Bo again said he did not know, fearful and ashamed, sweat soaking his back.

sentences.zh: 上問左丞相平。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Left Chancellor Ping.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked Left Chancellor Chen Ping.

sentences.zh: 平曰：「有主者。

translations.literal: Ping said, “There are those in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ping said, “There are officials in charge of that.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「主者謂誰？

translations.literal: ” The Emperor said, “Whom do you mean by those in charge?
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor said, “Who is in charge?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「陛下即問決獄，責廷尉；

translations.literal: ” He said, “If Your Majesty asks about deciding cases, hold the commandant of justice responsible;
translations.idiomatic: ” He said, “If Your Majesty asks about cases, hold the commandant of justice responsible;

sentences.zh: 問錢穀，責治粟內史。

translations.literal: if you ask about money and grain, hold the superintendent of grain within the passes responsible.
translations.idiomatic: if about money and grain, hold the superintendent of grain responsible.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「苟各有主者，而君所主者何事也？

translations.literal: ” The Emperor said, “If each has its charge, what affairs does the lord chancellor himself oversee?
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor said, “If each has its officer, what do you yourself oversee?

sentences.zh: 」平謝曰：「陛下不知其駑下，使待罪宰相。

translations.literal: ” Ping apologized, saying, “Your Majesty does not know my incompetence and has made me serve as chancellor while awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chen Ping apologized: “Your Majesty does not know how incompetent I am and has made me serve as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 宰相者，上佐天子，理陰陽，順四時；

translations.literal: The chancellor assists the Son of Heaven above, harmonizes yin and yang, and accords with the four seasons;
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor assists the Son of Heaven above, harmonizes yin and yang, and accords with the four seasons;

sentences.zh: 下遂萬物之宜；

translations.literal: below he carries through what is fitting for the ten thousand things;
translations.idiomatic: below he brings the ten thousand things to their proper course;

sentences.zh: 外鎮撫四夷諸侯；

translations.literal: externally he pacifies the four Yi and feudal lords;
translations.idiomatic: externally he pacifies the four quarters and feudal lords;

sentences.zh: 內親附百姓，使卿大夫各得任其職焉。

translations.literal: internally he draws the people close and causes ministers and grandees each to fulfill his charge.
translations.idiomatic: internally he draws the people close and sees that ministers and grandees each fulfill his charge.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃稱善。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor then praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor praised this.

sentences.zh: 右丞相大慚，出而讓陳平曰：「君獨不素教我對！

translations.literal: The right chancellor was greatly ashamed; going out he reproached Chen Ping, saying, “Did you alone never teach me how to answer!
translations.idiomatic: The right chancellor was deeply ashamed; leaving court he reproached Chen Ping: “Why did you never teach me how to answer!

sentences.zh: 」陳平笑曰：「君居其位，不知其任邪？

translations.literal: ” Chen Ping laughed and said, “You occupy the post—do you not know its charge?
translations.idiomatic: ” Chen Ping laughed: “You hold the post—do you not know its duties?

sentences.zh: 且陛下即問長安中盜賊數，君欲強對邪？

translations.literal: Moreover, if Your Majesty were to ask the number of thieves in Chang'an, would you force an answer?
translations.idiomatic: And if Your Majesty asked how many thieves there are in Chang'an, would you force an answer?

sentences.zh: 」於是絳侯自知其能不如平遠矣。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the Marquis of Jiang knew that his ability fell far short of Ping's.
translations.idiomatic: ” Then the Marquis of Jiang knew his ability fell far short of Chen Ping's.

sentences.zh: 居頃之，人或說勃曰：「君既誅諸呂，立代王，威震天下。

translations.literal: Before long someone urged Bo, saying, “You executed the Lü clan and established the King of Dai; your authority shakes the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Before long someone urged Zhou Bo: “You executed the Lü clan and established the King of Dai; your authority shakes the realm.

sentences.zh: 而君受厚賞，處尊位，久之，即禍及身矣。

translations.literal: Yet you received rich rewards and occupy an exalted post; before long disaster will reach your person.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you have received rich rewards and hold an exalted post; before long disaster will reach you.

sentences.zh: 」勃亦自危，乃謝病，請歸相印，上許之。

translations.literal: ” Bo also felt himself in peril; he then declined on grounds of illness and asked to return the chancellor's seal, and the Emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhou Bo also felt endangered; he declined on grounds of illness and asked to return the chancellor's seal, and the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，辛未，右丞相勃免，左丞相平專為丞相。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on xinwei, Right Chancellor Bo was dismissed and Left Chancellor Ping alone became chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on xinwei, Right Chancellor Zhou Bo was dismissed and Left Chancellor Chen Ping became sole chancellor.

sentences.zh: ----13初，隆慮侯灶擊南越，會暑濕，士卒大疫，兵不能隃領。

translations.literal: ----13 At first the Marquis of Longlü, Zao, attacked the Southern Yue; encountering heat and dampness, the troops suffered a great epidemic and the army could not cross the passes.
translations.idiomatic: ----13 Earlier, when the Marquis of Longlü, Zao, attacked the Southern Yue, heat and damp brought a great epidemic among the troops and the army could not cross the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，-{高后}-崩，即罷兵。

translations.literal: After more than a year -{高后}- died and the troops were at once withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year Empress Dowager Gao died and the army was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 趙佗因此以兵威財物賂遺閩越、西甌、駱，役屬焉。

translations.literal: Zhao Tuo thereby used military might and goods as bribes to present to Min Yue, Western Ou, and the Luo, and made them subject to his service.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tuo then used military might and gifts to win over Min Yue, Western Ou, and the Luo peoples and bring them under his rule.

sentences.zh: 東西萬餘里，乘黃屋左纛，稱制與中國侔。

translations.literal: East and west more than ten thousand li, he rode the yellow canopy with the left banner and styled himself emperor on a par with China.
translations.idiomatic: His domain stretched more than ten thousand li east to west; he rode the yellow canopy with the left banner and styled himself emperor on a par with China.

sentences.zh: 帝乃為佗親塚在真定者置守邑，歲時奉祀；

translations.literal: The Emperor then for Tuo's ancestral tombs at Zhending established guard districts and seasonal sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then established guard districts for Zhao Tuo's ancestral tombs at Zhending and ordered seasonal sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 召其昆弟，尊官、厚賜寵之。

translations.literal: summoned his brothers, gave them honored offices, and richly favored them.
translations.idiomatic: summoned his brothers, gave them honored posts, and richly favored them.

sentences.zh: 復使陸賈使南越，賜佗書曰：「朕，高皇帝側室之子也，棄外，奉北籓於代。

translations.literal: He again sent Lu Jia as envoy to the Southern Yue and bestowed on Tuo a letter saying, “We are a son of Gaozu by a side chamber, set aside abroad, and received the northern fief at Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent Lu Jia as envoy to the Southern Yue with a letter to Zhao Tuo: “I am a son of Gaozu by a concubine, set aside in the borderlands, and received the northern fief at Dai.

sentences.zh: 道里遼遠，壅蔽樸愚，未嘗致書。

translations.literal: The roads are far and communication blocked; crude and foolish, We have never sent a letter.
translations.idiomatic: The roads are distant and I was cut off in my simplicity; I have never before sent you word.

sentences.zh: 高皇帝棄群臣，孝惠皇帝即世；

translations.literal: Gaozu left his ministers; Emperor Xiaohui passed from the world;
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu left his ministers; Emperor Xiaohui passed away;

sentences.zh: -{高后}-自臨事，不幸有疾，諸呂為變，賴功臣之力，誅之已畢，朕以王、侯、吏不釋之故，不得不立。

translations.literal: -{高后}- herself oversaw affairs; unfortunately she fell ill and the Lü clan made trouble; relying on the merit of the great ministers they were executed to completion; We, because kings, marquises, and officials would not be released, had no choice but to take the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Gao herself held power; she fell ill and the Lü clan rebelled; thanks to the great ministers they were executed to the last; because kings, marquises, and officials would not be reassured, I had no choice but to ascend.

sentences.zh: 今即位。

translations.literal: Now We have taken the throne.
translations.idiomatic: I have now taken the throne.

sentences.zh: 乃者聞王遺將軍隆慮侯書，求親昆弟，請罷長沙兩將軍。

translations.literal: Recently We heard that Your Majesty sent a letter to General the Marquis of Longlü, seeking your kin among brothers and asking that the two generals of Changsha be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I heard that you sent a letter to General the Marquis of Longlü, seeking your brothers and asking that the two Changsha generals be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 朕以王書罷將軍博陽侯；

translations.literal: We, on account of Your Majesty's letter, dismissed General the Marquis of Boyang;
translations.idiomatic: At your request I have dismissed General the Marquis of Boyang;

sentences.zh: 親昆弟在真定者，已遣人存問，修治先人塚。

translations.literal: kinsmen and brothers at Zhending have already had men sent to inquire after them and repair the ancestral tombs.
translations.idiomatic: your brothers at Zhending have already been visited and your ancestral tombs repaired.

sentences.zh: 前日聞王發兵於邊，為寇災不止。

translations.literal: The other day We heard that Your Majesty raised troops on the border and raiding disasters have not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The other day I heard you had raised troops on the border and raids have not ceased.

sentences.zh: 當其時，長沙苦之，南郡尤甚。

translations.literal: At that time Changsha suffered bitterly and Nan commandery suffered most of all.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Changsha suffered bitterly and Nan commandery most of all.

sentences.zh: 雖王之國，庸獨利乎！

translations.literal: Though it is Your Majesty's state, could it alone profit?
translations.idiomatic: Though it is your own kingdom, can it alone benefit?

sentences.zh: 必多殺士卒，傷良將吏，寡人之妻，孤人之子，獨人父母，得一亡十，朕不忍為也。

translations.literal: It must multiply the killing of soldiers, wound good generals and officials, make men's wives widows, orphan men's sons, and bereave men's parents—for one gain ten losses; We cannot bear to do it.
translations.idiomatic: It must multiply the killing of soldiers, wound good commanders, widow wives, orphan sons, and bereave parents—for one gain, ten losses; I cannot bear to do it.

sentences.zh: 朕欲定地犬牙相入者，以問吏，吏曰：『高皇帝所以介長沙土也。

translations.literal: We wish to fix boundaries where territories interlock like a dog's teeth and asked the officials; the officials said, ‘This is how Gaozu divided the soil of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to fix the boundaries where our lands interlock like dog's teeth and asked the officials; they said, ‘This is how Gaozu divided the territory of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 』朕不得擅變焉。

translations.literal: ’ We cannot change it on Our own authority.
translations.idiomatic: ’ I cannot change that on my own authority.

sentences.zh: 今得王之地，不足以為大；

translations.literal: Now to gain Your Majesty's territory would not suffice to make one great;
translations.idiomatic: To take your territory would not make me great;

sentences.zh: 得王之財，不足以為富。

translations.literal: to gain Your Majesty's wealth would not suffice to make one rich.
translations.idiomatic: to take your wealth would not make me rich.

sentences.zh: 服領以南，王自治之。

translations.literal: South of Fuling Pass, Your Majesty may govern on your own.
translations.idiomatic: South of Fuling Pass you may govern on your own.

sentences.zh: 雖然，王之號為帝。

translations.literal: Nevertheless, Your Majesty's title is emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless, your title is still emperor.

sentences.zh: 兩帝並立，亡一乘之使以通其道，是爭也；

translations.literal: If two emperors stand side by side yet lack even a one-horse envoy to keep a road open between them, that is contention;
translations.idiomatic: If two emperors stand together yet lack even a one-horse messenger to keep the road open between them, that is contention;

sentences.zh: 爭而不讓，仁者不為也。

translations.literal: to contend and not yield—no benevolent man would do it.
translations.idiomatic: to contend and not yield—no benevolent man would do it.

sentences.zh: 願與王分棄前惡，終今以來，通使如故。

translations.literal: We wish with Your Majesty equally to cast aside past ill will; from this end forward, to send envoys as of old.
translations.idiomatic: I wish with you equally to cast aside past ill will; from now on let envoys pass as before.

sentences.zh: 賈至南越，南越王恐，頓首謝罪，願奉明詔，長為籓臣，奉貢職。

translations.literal: When Jia reached the Southern Yue, the King of Southern Yue was afraid; he knocked his head and apologized, willing to receive the bright edict and long be a frontier vassal, fulfilling tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Jia reached the Southern Yue, the king was afraid; he knocked his head in apology and vowed to obey the imperial edict, remain a frontier vassal forever, and fulfill his tribute duties.

sentences.zh: 於是下令國中曰：「吾聞兩雄不俱立，兩賢不並世。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued an order in the state, saying, “I have heard that two heroes do not stand together, nor two sages in one age.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he issued an order throughout the state: “I have heard that two heroes do not stand together, nor two sages in one age.

sentences.zh: 漢皇帝，賢天子。

translations.literal: The Han Emperor is a worthy Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Emperor is a worthy Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 自今以來，去帝制、黃屋、左纛。

translations.literal: From this end forward, abandon the imperial system, yellow canopy, and left banner.
translations.idiomatic: From now on I shall abandon the imperial title, yellow canopy, and left banner.

sentences.zh: 」因為書，稱：「蠻夷大長、老夫臣佗昧死再拜上書皇帝陛下：老夫，故越吏也，高皇帝幸賜臣佗璽，以為南越王。

translations.literal: ” He then composed a letter, styled: “Great chieftain of the barbarian Yi, your old servant Tuo, risking death, twice knocks head and submits this letter to His Majesty the Emperor: I, your old servant, was formerly a Yue official; the High Emperor graciously granted me Tuo a seal and made me King of the Southern Yue.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then wrote a letter styled: “Great chieftain of the barbarians, your old servant Tuo, risking death, twice knocks head and submits this letter to His Majesty the Emperor: I, your old servant, was formerly a Yue official; the High Emperor graciously granted me a seal and made me King of the Southern Yue.

sentences.zh: 孝惠皇帝即位，義不忍絕，所以賜老夫者甚厚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaohui took the throne, in righteousness he could not bear to cut me off, and what he bestowed on me, your old servant, was very generous.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaohui took the throne, in righteousness he could not cut me off, and what he bestowed on your old servant was very generous.

sentences.zh: -{高后}-用事，別異蠻夷，出令曰：『毋與蠻夷越金、鐵、田器、馬、牛、羊。

translations.literal: -{高后}- held power, treated the barbarian Yi differently, and issued an order, saying, ‘Do not give the barbarian Yi of Yue gold, iron, field tools, horses, cattle, or sheep.
translations.idiomatic: -{高后}- held power, treated the barbarians differently, and issued an order: ‘Do not give the barbarian Yi of Yue gold, iron, field tools, horses, cattle, or sheep.

sentences.zh: 即予，予牡，毋予牝。

translations.literal: If you give any, give males; do not give females.
translations.idiomatic: If you give any, give males only; do not give females.

sentences.zh: 』老夫處僻，馬、牛、羊齒已長。

translations.literal: ’ Your old servant dwells in a remote place; our horses, cattle, and sheep are already grown.
translations.idiomatic: ’ Your old servant dwells in a remote place; our horses, cattle, and sheep are already fully grown.

sentences.zh: 自以祭祀不修，有死罪，使內史籓、中尉高、御史平凡三輩上書謝過，皆不反。

translations.literal: Thinking ritual sacrifice poorly kept was a capital offense, I sent three parties—the inner secretary Fan, commandant of the guards Gao, and common recorder Ping of the censorate—to submit letters apologizing; none returned.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking that poorly kept sacrifices were a capital offense, I sent three parties—the inner secretary Fan, the commandant of the guards Gao, and the censorate recorder Ping—to submit letters of apology; none returned.

sentences.zh: 又風聞老夫父母墳墓已壞削，兄弟宗族已誅論。

translations.literal: I also heard on rumor that my parents' tombs had been destroyed and my brothers and clansmen condemned and executed.
translations.idiomatic: I also heard on rumor that my parents' tombs had been destroyed and my brothers and clansmen condemned and executed.

sentences.zh: 吏相與議曰：『今內不得振於漢，外無以自高異。

translations.literal: Officials discussed among themselves, saying, ‘Now inwardly we cannot gain standing with Han, and outwardly have no way to exalt ourselves differently.
translations.idiomatic: Officials discussed among themselves: ‘Now inwardly we cannot gain standing with Han, and outwardly have no way to set ourselves apart.

sentences.zh: 』故更號為帝，自帝其國，非敢有害於天下。

translations.literal: ’ So we changed our title to emperor and made ourselves emperors in our state—not daring to harm all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ’ So we changed our title to emperor and styled ourselves emperors in our state—not daring to harm all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 高皇后聞之，大怒，削去南越之籍，使使不通。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Gao heard, she was greatly angry, struck Southern Yue from the register, and cut off envoys.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Gao heard, she was greatly angry, struck Southern Yue from the register, and cut off diplomatic contact.

sentences.zh: 老夫竊疑長沙王讒臣，故發兵以伐其邊。

translations.literal: Your old servant privately suspected the King of Changsha had slandered me, so I sent troops to attack his border.
translations.idiomatic: Your old servant privately suspected the King of Changsha had slandered me, so I sent troops to raid his border.

sentences.zh: 老夫處越四十九年，於今抱孫焉。

translations.literal: Your old servant has dwelt in Yue forty-nine years and now holds a grandchild in his arms.
translations.idiomatic: Your old servant has dwelt in Yue forty-nine years and now holds a grandchild in his arms.

sentences.zh: 然夙興夜寐，寢不安席，食不甘味，目不視靡曼之色，耳不聽鐘鼓之音者，以不得事漢也。

translations.literal: Yet rising early and sleeping late, bed without peace, food without savor, eyes not viewing gorgeous colors, ears not hearing bells and drums—all because I could not serve Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rising early and sleeping late, with no peace in bed or savor in food, eyes not viewing gorgeous colors, ears not hearing bells and drums—all because I could not serve Han.

sentences.zh: 今陛下幸哀憐，復故號，通使漢如故；

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has graciously pitied me, restored the old title, and envoys with Han as before;
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has graciously pitied me, restored my old title, and envoys pass with Han as before;

sentences.zh: 老夫死，骨不腐。

translations.literal: when your old servant dies, his bones will not rot away.
translations.idiomatic: when your old servant dies, his bones will not rot away.

sentences.zh: 改號，不敢為帝矣！

translations.literal: To change our title—I dare not be emperor again!
translations.idiomatic: To change our title—I dare not be emperor again!”

translations.literal: ” ----14 King Ai of Qi, Xiang, died.
translations.idiomatic: ” ----14 King Ai of Qi, Liu Xiang, died.

sentences.zh: ----15上聞河南守吳公治平為天下第一，召以為廷尉。

translations.literal: ----15 The Emperor heard that Wu Gong, prefect of Henan, in governance and peace ranked first in all under Heaven and summoned him to be commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: ----15 The Emperor heard that Wu Gong, prefect of Henan, ranked first in all under Heaven for governance and peace, and summoned him to be commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 吳公薦洛陽人賈誼，帝召以為博士。

translations.literal: Wu Gong recommended Jia Yi of Luoyang; the Emperor summoned him and made him erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Gong recommended Jia Yi of Luoyang; the Emperor summoned him and made him an erudite.

sentences.zh: 是時賈生年二十餘。

translations.literal: At that time Master Jia was in his twenties.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jia Yi was in his twenties.

sentences.zh: 帝愛其辭博，一歲中，超遷至太中大夫。

translations.literal: The Emperor loved his broad eloquence; within a year he was promoted past regular steps to grand master of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor loved his broad learning; within a year he was promoted past regular steps to grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 賈生請改正朔，易服色，定官名，興禮樂，以立漢制，更秦法。

translations.literal: Master Jia asked to correct the calendar beginning, change ceremonial colors, fix official titles, raise ritual and music, establish Han institutions, and reform Qin law.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi asked to correct the calendar, change ceremonial colors, fix official titles, raise ritual and music, establish Han institutions, and reform Qin law.

sentences.zh: 帝謙讓未遑也。

translations.literal: The Emperor modestly deferred—there was as yet no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor modestly deferred; there was as yet no leisure for it.

sentences.zh: ----1冬，十月，曲逆獻侯陳平薨。

translations.literal: ----1 In winter, the tenth month, Marquis Xian of Quyu, Chen Ping, died.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In winter, the tenth month, Marquis Xian of Quyu, Chen Ping, died.

sentences.zh: ----2詔列侯各之國，為吏及詔所止者，遣太子。

translations.literal: ----2 An edict: feudal lords each to their states; those serving as officials and those halted by edict should send their heirs.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 An edict ordered feudal lords each to his state; those serving as officials and those held back by edict were to send their heirs.

sentences.zh: ----3十一月，乙亥，周勃復為丞相。

translations.literal: ----3 In the eleventh month, on yihai, Zhou Bo again became chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In the eleventh month, on yihai, Zhou Bo again became chancellor.

sentences.zh: ----4癸卯晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: ----4 On the last day of the month guimao, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 On the last day of the month guimao, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 詔：「群臣悉思朕之過失及知見之所不及，匄以啟告朕。

translations.literal: An edict: “Let all ministers reflect on Our faults and what their knowledge and insight fail to reach, and beg to report them to Us.
translations.idiomatic: An edict: “Let all ministers reflect on my faults and on what their knowledge and insight fail to reach, and beg to report them to me.

sentences.zh: 及舉賢良、方正、能直言極諫者，以匡朕之不逮。

translations.literal: And recommend worthy and upright men able to speak bluntly and remonstrate extremely, to correct Our shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: And recommend worthy and upright men able to speak bluntly and remonstrate forcefully, to correct my shortcomings.

sentences.zh: 」因各敕以職任，務省繇費以便民，罷衛將軍。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon each was charged with his duties, charged to reduce corvée levies to benefit the people, and the general of the guard was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: ” Thereupon each was charged with his duties, told to reduce corvée levies to benefit the people, and the general of the guard was abolished.

sentences.zh: 太僕見馬遺財足，餘皆以給傳置。

translations.literal: The grand coachman reported surplus horses at the treasury; the remainder were all given to relay stations.
translations.idiomatic: The grand coachman reported surplus horses in the treasury; the remainder were all assigned to relay stations.

sentences.zh: 穎陰侯騎賈山上書言治亂之道曰：

translations.literal: The Marquis of Yingyin, Jia Shan, submitted a memorial on the Way of order and disorder, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Yingyin, Jia Shan, submitted a memorial on the way of order and disorder, saying:

sentences.zh: :「臣聞雷霆之所擊，無不摧折者；

translations.literal: : “I have heard that what thunderbolts strike, nothing fails to be shattered;
translations.idiomatic: : “I have heard that what thunderbolts strike, nothing fails to be shattered;

sentences.zh: 萬鈞之所壓，無不糜滅者。

translations.literal: what ten thousand jun weights press, nothing fails to be ground to dust.
translations.idiomatic: what ten thousand jun weights press, nothing fails to be ground to dust.

sentences.zh: 今人主之威，非特雷霆也；

translations.literal: Now the lord's majesty is not merely like thunderbolts;
translations.idiomatic: Now the lord's majesty is not merely like thunderbolts;

sentences.zh: 執重，非特萬鈞也。

translations.literal: what he grasps is weighty—not merely ten thousand jun.
translations.idiomatic: what he holds is weighty—not merely ten thousand jun.

sentences.zh: 開道而求諫，和顏色而受之，用其言而顯其身，士猶恐懼而不敢自盡；

translations.literal: He opens the Way and seeks remonstrance, receives it with gentle countenance, uses their words and honors their persons—yet scholars still fear and dare not exhaust themselves;
translations.idiomatic: He opens the way and seeks remonstrance, receives it with a gentle countenance, uses their words and honors their persons—yet scholars still fear and dare not speak their full mind;

sentences.zh: 又況於縱欲恣暴、惡聞其過乎！

translations.literal: how much more when one indulges desires, acts willfully and violently, and hates to hear of one's faults!
translations.idiomatic: how much more when one indulges desire, acts willfully and violently, and hates to hear of one's faults!

sentences.zh: 震之以威，壓之以重，雖有堯、舜之智，孟賁之勇，豈有不摧折者哉！

translations.literal: Shake them with majesty, press them with weight—even with Yao and Shun's wisdom, Meng Ben's courage, would there be any who are not shattered!
translations.idiomatic: Shake them with majesty and press them with weight—even with the wisdom of Yao and Shun and the courage of Meng Ben, would any fail to be shattered!

sentences.zh: 如此，則人主不得聞其過，社稷危矣。

translations.literal: If so, the lord cannot hear his faults and the altars of state are in peril.
translations.idiomatic: If so, the lord cannot hear his faults and the altars of state are in peril.

sentences.zh: :昔者周蓋千八百國，以九州之民養千八百國之君，君有餘財，民有餘力，而頌聲作。

translations.literal: : In former times Zhou had perhaps eighteen hundred states; the people of the Nine Provinces supported eighteen hundred lords—the lords had surplus wealth, the people surplus strength, and songs of praise arose.
translations.idiomatic: : In former times Zhou had perhaps eighteen hundred states; the people of the Nine Provinces supported eighteen hundred lords—the lords had surplus wealth, the people surplus strength, and songs of praise arose.

sentences.zh: 秦皇帝以千八百國之民自養，力罷不能勝其役，財盡不能勝其求。

translations.literal: The Qin Emperor used the people of those eighteen hundred states to nourish himself alone; strength exhausted, they could not bear his corvées; wealth spent, they could not satisfy his demands.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor of Qin used the people of those eighteen hundred states to nourish himself alone; strength exhausted, they could not bear his corvées; wealth spent, they could not satisfy his demands.

sentences.zh: 一君之身耳，所自養者馳騁弋獵之娛，天下弗能供也。

translations.literal: One lord's person—the pleasures he nourished himself with were racing, archery, and hunting—and all under Heaven could not supply them.
translations.idiomatic: One man's person—the pleasures with which he nourished himself were racing, archery, and hunting—and all under Heaven could not supply them.

sentences.zh: 秦皇帝計其功德，度其後嗣世世無窮；

translations.literal: The First Emperor of Qin reckoned his merit and measured that his descendants for generations without end—
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor reckoned his merit and measured that his descendants for generations without end—

sentences.zh: 然身死才數月耳，天下四面而攻之，宗廟滅絕矣。

translations.literal: yet within only a few months after his death all under Heaven attacked from four sides and the ancestral temple was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: yet within only a few months after his death all under Heaven attacked from four sides and the ancestral temple was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 秦皇帝居滅絕之中而不自知者，何也？

translations.literal: The First Emperor of Qin dwelt in extinction yet did not know it—why?
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor dwelt in extinction yet did not know it—why?

sentences.zh: 天下莫敢告也。

translations.literal: All under Heaven dared not tell him.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven dared not tell him.

sentences.zh: 其所以莫敢告者，何也？

translations.literal: Why did none dare tell him?
translations.idiomatic: Why did none dare tell him?

sentences.zh: 亡養老之義，亡輔弼之臣，退誹謗之人，殺直諫之士。

translations.literal: He lacked the duty of nurturing the aged, lacked ministers who assisted and supported, dismissed those who criticized, and killed those who spoke bluntly.
translations.idiomatic: He lacked the duty of nurturing the aged, lacked assisting ministers, dismissed those who criticized, and killed those who spoke bluntly.

sentences.zh: 是以道諛、媮合苟容，比其德則賢於堯、舜，課其功則賢於湯、武；

translations.literal: Thus the way of flattery and shameless compliance: compared in virtue he surpassed Yao and Shun; judged in achievement he surpassed Tang and Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the way of flattery and shameless compliance: in comparing his virtue he surpassed Yao and Shun; in judging his achievement he surpassed Tang and Wu;

sentences.zh: 天下已潰而莫之告也。

translations.literal: all under Heaven had already collapsed yet none told him.
translations.idiomatic: all under Heaven had already collapsed yet none told him.

sentences.zh: :今陛下使天下舉賢良方正之士，天下皆欣欣焉曰：『將興堯舜之道、三王之功矣。

translations.literal: : Now Your Majesty has caused all under Heaven to recommend worthy and upright men; all under Heaven rejoice and say, ‘He is about to raise the Way of Yao and Shun and the achievement of the Three Kings.
translations.idiomatic: : Now Your Majesty has caused all under Heaven to recommend worthy and upright men; all under Heaven rejoice and say, ‘He is about to raise the way of Yao and Shun and the achievement of the Three Kings.

sentences.zh: 』天下之士，莫不精白以承休德。

translations.literal: ’ Scholars everywhere none fail to refine themselves to receive your gracious virtue.
translations.idiomatic: ’ Scholars everywhere refine themselves to receive your gracious virtue.

sentences.zh: 今方正之士皆在朝廷矣；

translations.literal: Now worthy and upright men are all at court;
translations.idiomatic: Now worthy and upright men are all at court;

sentences.zh: 又選其賢者，使為常侍、諸吏，與之馳驅射獵，一日再三出。

translations.literal: and choosing the worthiest among them, you make them attendants-in-ordinary and various officials and ride and hunt with them—going out three or four times in a day.
translations.idiomatic: yet choosing the worthiest among them, you make them attendants-in-ordinary and various officials and ride and hunt with them—going out three or four times in a day.

sentences.zh: 臣恐朝廷之解馳，百官之墮於事也。

translations.literal: I fear the court will grow slack and hundreds of officials fall behind in their duties.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the court will grow slack and the hundred officials will neglect their duties.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位，親自勉以厚天下，節用愛民，平獄緩刑；

translations.literal: Your Majesty since taking the throne has personally urged thickening all under Heaven, sparing expense and loving the people, leveling prisons and easing punishments;
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the throne you have personally urged enriching all under Heaven, sparing expense and loving the people, leveling prisons and easing punishments;

sentences.zh: 天下莫不說喜。

translations.literal: and all under Heaven none fail to delight.
translations.idiomatic: and all under Heaven rejoices.

sentences.zh: 臣聞山東吏布詔令，民雖老羸癃疾，扶杖而往聽之，願少須臾毋死，思見德化之成也。

translations.literal: I hear that when officers east of the mountains issued edicts, people though old, frail, and crippled leaned on staves to go listen, wishing to live a little longer without dying to see your transforming virtue fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that when officers east of the mountains issued edicts, people though old, frail, and crippled leaned on staves to go and listen, wishing to live a little longer without dying to see your transforming virtue fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 今功業方就，名聞方昭，四方鄉風而從；

translations.literal: Now your achievement is just being completed and your fame just spreading—the four quarters look to your wind and follow;
translations.idiomatic: Now your achievement is just being completed and your fame just spreading—the four quarters look to your example and follow;

sentences.zh: 豪俊之臣，方正之士，直與之日日獵射，擊兔、伐狐，以傷大業，絕天下之望，臣竊悼之。

translations.literal: yet worthy grandees and upright scholars go straight to daily hunting and shooting, striking rabbits and killing foxes, injuring the great work and cutting off all under Heaven's hopes—I mourn it privately.
translations.idiomatic: yet worthy grandees and upright scholars go straight to daily hunting and shooting, striking rabbits and killing foxes, injuring the great work and cutting off all under Heaven's hopes—I mourn it privately.

sentences.zh: 古者大臣不得與宴游，使皆務其方而高其節，則群臣莫敢不正身修行，盡心以稱大體。

translations.literal: In antiquity great ministers did not join in feasting and outings; making all devote themselves to their duties and elevate their integrity, then no minister dared fail to straighten body and cultivate conduct and give full heart to match the great framework.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity great ministers did not join in feasting and outings; if all were made to devote themselves to their duties and elevate their integrity, then no minister would dare fail to straighten his conduct and give full heart to match the great framework.

sentences.zh: 夫士，修之於家而壞之於天子之廷，臣竊愍之。

translations.literal: Scholars refined at home yet ruined in the Son of Heaven's court—I pity it privately.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars refined at home yet ruined in the Son of Heaven's court—I pity it privately.

sentences.zh: 陛下與眾臣宴游，與大臣、方正朝廷論議，游不失樂，朝不失禮，議不失計，軌事之大者也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should feast and recreate with the multitude of ministers, but debate policy in court with great ministers and upright men—outing without losing pleasure, court without losing ritual, debate without losing plans: these are the great tracks of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should feast and recreate with the multitude of ministers, but debate policy in court with great ministers and upright men—outing without losing pleasure, court without losing ritual, debate without losing plans: these are the great tracks of affairs.

sentences.zh: 上嘉納其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and adopted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised and adopted his words.

sentences.zh: 上每朝，郎、從官上書疏，未嘗不止輦受其言。

translations.literal: At each audience the Emperor, when gentlemen and attendant officials submitted memorials, never failed to stop the palanquin and receive their words.
translations.idiomatic: At each audience, when gentlemen and attendant officials submitted memorials, the Emperor never failed to stop the palanquin and receive their words.

sentences.zh: 言不可用置之，言可用采之，未嘗不稱善。

translations.literal: What could not be used he set aside; what could be used he adopted—he never failed to say it was good.
translations.idiomatic: What could not be used he set aside; what could be used he adopted—he never failed to praise it as good.

sentences.zh: 帝從霸陵上欲西馳下峻阪。

translations.literal: The Emperor, coming from over Baling Ridge, wished to gallop westward down a steep slope.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, riding over Baling Ridge, wished to gallop westward down a steep slope.

sentences.zh: 中郎將袁盎騎，並車攬轡。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Gentlemen Yuan Ang rode alongside, drew abreast, and pulled the reins.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of the Gentlemen Yuan Ang rode alongside, drew abreast of the chariot, and pulled the reins.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「將軍怯邪？

translations.literal: The Emperor said, “General, are you afraid?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, “General, are you afraid?

sentences.zh: 」盎曰：「臣聞『千金之子，坐不垂堂』。

translations.literal: ” Ang said, “I have heard, ‘A son worth a thousand in gold does not sit where the eaves overhang.’
translations.idiomatic: ” Yuan Ang said, “I have heard, ‘A son worth a thousand in gold does not sit beneath overhanging eaves.’

sentences.zh: 聖主不乘危，不徼幸。

translations.literal: A sage lord does not ride in peril or court luck.
translations.idiomatic: A sage lord does not ride in peril or court luck.

sentences.zh: 今陛下騁六飛馳下峻山，有如馬驚車敗，陛下縱自輕，奈高廟、太后何！

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty would gallop the six-horse team down a steep mountain—if the horses startle and the chariot breaks, though Your Majesty might make light of yourself, what of the High Ancestor's temple and the empress dowager!
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty would gallop the six-horse team down a steep mountain—if the horses startle and the chariot breaks, though Your Majesty might make light of yourself, what of the High Ancestor's temple and the empress dowager!

sentences.zh: 」上乃止。

translations.literal: ” The Emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Emperor then stopped.

sentences.zh: 上所幸慎夫人，在禁中常與皇后同席坐。

translations.literal: Consort Shen, whom the Emperor favored, in the inner palace often sat on the same mat as the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Shen, whom the Emperor favored, in the inner palace often sat on the same mat as the empress.

sentences.zh: 及坐郎置，袁盎引卻慎夫人坐。

translations.literal: When they sat with attendants arranged, Yuan Ang drew back Consort Shen's seat.
translations.idiomatic: When they sat with attendants in place, Yuan Ang drew back Consort Shen's seat.

sentences.zh: 慎夫人怒，不肯坐；

translations.literal: Consort Shen was angry and would not sit;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Shen was angry and would not sit;

sentences.zh: 上亦怒，起，入禁中。

translations.literal: the Emperor too was angry, rose, and went into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor too was angry, rose, and went into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 盎因前說曰：「臣聞『尊卑有序，則上下和』。

translations.literal: Ang then advanced and said, “I have heard, ‘When high and low are ordered, then above and below are harmonized.’
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ang then advanced and said, “I have heard, ‘When high and low are ordered, then above and below are harmonized.’

sentences.zh: 今陛下既已立-{后}-，慎夫人乃妾。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has already established -{后}-; Consort Shen is but a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has already established -{后}-; Consort Shen is but a concubine.

sentences.zh: 妾、主豈可與同坐哉！

translations.literal: How can concubine and mistress sit together!
translations.idiomatic: How can a concubine and the mistress sit together!

sentences.zh: 且陛下幸之，即厚賜之。

translations.literal: Moreover, if Your Majesty favors her, richly reward her—
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if Your Majesty favors her, richly reward her—

sentences.zh: 陛下所以為慎夫人，適所以禍之也。

translations.literal: what Your Majesty does for Consort Shen is exactly what will bring calamity upon her.
translations.idiomatic: what Your Majesty does for Consort Shen is exactly what will bring calamity upon her.

sentences.zh: 陛下獨不見『人彘』乎！

translations.literal: Has Your Majesty alone not seen the ‘human pig’!
translations.idiomatic: Has Your Majesty alone not seen the ‘human pig’!

sentences.zh: 」於是上乃說，召語慎夫人，慎夫人賜盎金五十斤。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the Emperor was persuaded, summoned and told Consort Shen, and Consort Shen bestowed fifty jin of gold on Ang.
translations.idiomatic: ” Thereupon the Emperor was persuaded, summoned Consort Shen and spoke to her, and Consort Shen bestowed fifty jin of gold on Yuan Ang.

sentences.zh: 賈誼說上曰：

translations.literal: Jia Yi spoke to the Emperor, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi spoke to the Emperor, saying:

sentences.zh: :「《管子》曰：『倉廩實而知禮節，衣食足而知榮辱。

translations.literal: : “The Guanzi says, ‘When granaries are full, then ritual and propriety are known; when clothing and food are sufficient, then honor and shame are known.
translations.idiomatic: : “The Guanzi says, ‘When granaries are full, then ritual and propriety are known; when clothing and food are sufficient, then honor and shame are known.

sentences.zh: 』民不足而可治者，自古及今，未之嘗聞。

translations.literal: ’ That the people are insufficient yet the state can be governed—from antiquity until now, none has ever heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: ’ That the people are insufficient yet the state can be governed—from antiquity until now, none has ever heard of it.

sentences.zh: 古之人曰：『一夫不耕，或受之饑；

translations.literal: The men of antiquity said: ‘If one man does not plow, someone may suffer hunger from it;
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: ‘If one man does not plow, someone may go hungry;

sentences.zh: 一女不織，或受之寒。

translations.literal: if one woman does not weave, someone may suffer cold from it.
translations.idiomatic: if one woman does not weave, someone may go cold.

sentences.zh: 』生之有時而用之亡度，則物力必屈。

translations.literal: ’ Birth has its seasons yet use is without measure—then material power must be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: ’ Production has its seasons, yet consumption knows no limit—then material resources must fail.

sentences.zh: 古之治天下，至纖至悉，故其畜積足恃。

translations.literal: In antiquity in governing all under Heaven it was most minute and most thorough; therefore their stored accumulations could be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity those who governed the realm were thorough to the finest detail, so their stored reserves could be trusted.

sentences.zh: 今背本而趨末者甚眾，是天下之大殘也！

translations.literal: Now those who turn their backs on the root and rush to the tip are very many—this is the great mutilator of all under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Today many abandon the fundamental and rush to the secondary—this is the great destroyer of the realm!

sentences.zh: 淫侈之俗，日日以長，是天下之大賊也！

translations.literal: The custom of dissipation and extravagance grows day by day—this is the great thief of all under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: The habit of excess and extravagance grows daily—this is the great thief of the realm!

sentences.zh: 殘、賊公行，莫之或止；

translations.literal: The mutilator and thief walk abroad openly, and none halt them;
translations.idiomatic: Destroyer and thief go unchecked, and no one stops them;

sentences.zh: 大命將泛，莫之振救。

translations.literal: the great mandate is about to be flooded away, and none rouses to save it.
translations.idiomatic: the nation's vital strength is about to fail, and no one stirs to rescue it.

sentences.zh: 生之者甚少而靡之者甚多，天下財產何得不厥。

translations.literal: Those who produce are very few while those who waste are very many—how can the wealth and goods of all under Heaven not be exhausted?
translations.idiomatic: Producers are few and spenders many—how can the realm's wealth not be depleted?

sentences.zh: :漢之為漢，幾四十年矣，公私之積，猶可哀痛。

translations.literal: : Han as Han has been almost forty years, yet public and private accumulations are still pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: : The Han dynasty has ruled for nearly forty years, yet public and private stores remain pitifully thin.

sentences.zh: 失時不雨，民且狼顧；

translations.literal: If the seasons miss their rain, the people will look back like wolves;
translations.idiomatic: If the seasons fail and rains do not come, the people will look about in alarm;

sentences.zh: 歲惡不入，請賣爵子。

translations.literal: if the harvest is bad and dues do not come in, they beg to sell rank and children.
translations.idiomatic: if the harvest fails and taxes cannot be paid, they beg to sell their noble ranks and even their children.

sentences.zh: 既聞耳矣，安有為天下阽危者若是而上不驚者！

translations.literal: This has already reached Our ears—how can there be one who brings all under Heaven to the brink such as this while those above are not alarmed!
translations.idiomatic: This has already reached my ears—how can the realm be brought to such peril while those above are not alarmed!

sentences.zh: :世之有饑、穰，天之行也；

translations.literal: : Famine and abundance in the world are Heaven's course;
translations.idiomatic: : Famine and plenty in the world are Heaven's way;

sentences.zh: 禹、湯被之矣。

translations.literal: Yu and Tang suffered them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and Tang endured them.

sentences.zh: 即不幸有方二三千里之旱，國胡以相恤？

translations.literal: If by misfortune there is drought over a region of two or three thousand li, with what will the state aid one another?
translations.idiomatic: If misfortune brings drought across two or three thousand li, how will the state aid one another?

sentences.zh: 卒然邊境有急，數十百萬之眾，國胡以饋之？

translations.literal: If suddenly the border has an emergency and hosts of hundreds of thousands and millions— with what will the state feed them?
translations.idiomatic: If suddenly the border is threatened and armies of hundreds of thousands or millions must be fed, with what will the state supply them?

sentences.zh: 兵、旱相乘，天下大屈，有勇力者聚徒而衡擊，罷夫、羸老，易子上咬其骨。

translations.literal: When war and drought multiply each other, all under Heaven is greatly depleted; men of courage and strength gather gangs and strike horizontally, exhausted husbands and frail old men exchange sons and gnaw their bones.
translations.idiomatic: When war and drought strike together, the realm is drained; the strong gather bands and rampage, while the worn-out and the aged exchange sons and gnaw on bones.

sentences.zh: 政治未畢通也，遠方之能僭擬者並舉而爭起矣；

translations.literal: Government is not yet fully communicated, and those in distant places who can usurp and imitate will together rise competing;
translations.idiomatic: Before government is fully restored, distant men who would usurp the throne will rise together in rivalry;

sentences.zh: 乃駭而圖之，豈將有及乎！

translations.literal: only then in alarm will one scheme—is there still time to reach it?
translations.idiomatic: only then in alarm will you take counsel—will it still be in time!

sentences.zh: 夫積貯者，天下之大命也。

translations.literal: Accumulated stores are the great mandate of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Stored grain is the lifeblood of the realm.

sentences.zh: 苟粟多而財有餘，何為而不成！

translations.literal: If grain is abundant and wealth has surplus, what doing would not succeed!
translations.idiomatic: If grain is plentiful and resources ample, what undertaking would not succeed!

sentences.zh: 以攻則取，以守則固，以戰則勝，懷敵附遠，何招而不至！

translations.literal: In attack one takes, in defense one is firm, in battle one wins; cherishing enemies and drawing distant ones near—what summons would not arrive!
translations.idiomatic: In attack you prevail, in defense you stand firm, in battle you win; win over foes and draw the distant near—what invitation would they not answer!

sentences.zh: :今驅民而歸之農，皆著於本。

translations.literal: : Now drive the people back to agriculture and all attach to the root.
translations.idiomatic: : Now drive the people back to farming and fix them all on the fundamental.

sentences.zh: 使天下各食其力，末技、游食之民轉而緣南晦則畜積足而人樂其所矣。

translations.literal: Make all under Heaven each eat by his labor; those of trivial skills and wandering eaters turn instead to attach to south hui—then stored accumulation is sufficient and men rejoice in their stations.
translations.idiomatic: Let all under Heaven live by their own labor; let those in petty crafts and idle wandering turn to the south-facing fields—then stores will be full and the people content in their places.

sentences.zh: 可以為富安天下，而直為此廩廩也，竊為陛下惜之！

translations.literal: One could thereby enrich and settle all under Heaven, yet Your Majesty simply lets granaries run this meager—I privately grieve for Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: By this you could enrich and secure the realm, yet Your Majesty lets the granaries run so thin—I grieve for you in private!

sentences.zh: 上感誼言，春，正月，丁亥，詔開藉田，上親耕以率天下之民。

translations.literal: The Emperor was moved by Yi's words; in spring, the first month, on dinghai, an edict opened the sacred field; the Emperor personally plowed to lead the people of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was moved by Jia Yi's words; in spring, the first month, on dinghai, an edict opened the sacred plowing field and the Emperor farmed in person to lead the people of the realm.

sentences.zh: ----5三月，有司請立皇子為諸侯王。

translations.literal: ----5 In the third month the responsible officials asked to establish the imperial sons as feudal kings.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In the third month officials asked that the imperial sons be enfeoffed as feudal kings.

sentences.zh: 詔先立趙幽王少子辟強為河間王，朱虛侯章為城陽王，東牟侯興居為濟北王；

translations.literal: An edict first established the young son of King You of Zhao, Piqiang, as King of Hejian; the Marquis of Zhu Xu, Zhang, as King of Chengyang; the Marquis of Dongmou, Xingju, as King of Jibei;
translations.idiomatic: An edict first made the young son of King You of Zhao, Piqiang, King of Hejian; the Marquis of Zhu Xu, Zhang, King of Chengyang; and the Marquis of Dongmou, Xingju, King of Jibei;

sentences.zh: 然後立皇子武為代王，參為太原王，揖為梁王。

translations.literal: then established the imperial son Wu as King of Dai, Can as King of Taiyuan, and Yi as King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: then made the imperial sons Wu King of Dai, Can King of Taiyuan, and Yi King of Liang.

sentences.zh: ----6五月，詔曰：「古之治天下，朝有進善之旌，誹謗之木，所以通治道而來諫者也。

translations.literal: ----6 In the fifth month an edict said: “In antiquity in governing all under Heaven, at court there were banners for advancing goodness and posts for slander—by these the way of governance was communicated and remonstrance brought in.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In the fifth month an edict said: “In antiquity those who governed the realm set up banners to reward good counsel and posts for criticism, so that the way of rule was kept open and remonstrance could reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 今法有誹謗、妖言之罪，是使眾臣不敢盡情而上無由聞過失也，將何以來遠方之賢良！

translations.literal: Now the law has crimes of slander and demon talk—this makes the multitude of ministers not dare speak fully while those above have no means to hear faults; with what will worthy and good men from afar be brought in!
translations.idiomatic: Now the law punishes slander and ‘demon talk,’ so ministers dare not speak plainly and those above have no way to hear their faults—how will worthy men from afar be drawn in!

sentences.zh: 其除之！

translations.literal: Let them be abolished!
translations.idiomatic: Abolish them!

sentences.zh: 」----7九月，詔曰：「農，天下之大本也，民所恃以生也；

translations.literal: ” ----7 In the ninth month an edict said: “Agriculture is the great root of all under Heaven, what the people rely on to live;
translations.idiomatic: ” ----7 In the ninth month an edict said: “Agriculture is the great foundation of the realm; the people depend on it for their livelihood;

sentences.zh: 而民或不務本而事末，故生不遂。

translations.literal: yet the people sometimes do not attend to the root but serve the tip, therefore life does not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: yet some neglect the root and pursue the secondary, so their livelihood fails.

sentences.zh: 朕憂其然，故今茲親率群臣農以勸之；

translations.literal: We worry at this; therefore now We personally lead the great ministers in farming to encourage it;
translations.idiomatic: I am troubled by this, and therefore now personally lead the ministers in farming to encourage it;

sentences.zh: 其賜天下民今年田租之半。

translations.literal: let half this year's field tax for the people of all under Heaven be bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: grant the people of the realm half this year's land tax.

sentences.zh: 」----8燕敬王澤薨。

translations.literal: ” ----8 King Jing of Yan, Ze, died.
translations.idiomatic: ” ----8 King Jing of Yan, Liu Ze, died.
